title: Busan vs Jeju: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Busan for city energy, seafood, and no-car convenience. Jeju for nature, volcanic landscapes, and beach beauty. Do both if you have 7+ days.

categories.name: Food and Dining
categories.summary: Busan has Jagalchi seafood and dwaeji gukbap. Jeju has black pork and haenyeo-caught abalone.

categories.name: Beaches
categories.summary: Jeju wins on natural beauty (Hyeopjae, Hamdeok). Busan wins on urban beach vibe (Haeundae, Gwangalli).

categories.name: Nature and Outdoors
categories.summary: Jeju has Hallasan volcano, Seongsan Ilchulbong, and lava caves.

categories.name: Getting Around
categories.summary: Busan has excellent subway. Jeju requires rental car and IDP.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Busan ~150,000 KRW/day. Jeju ~220,000 KRW/day including car.

categories.name: Nightlife
categories.summary: Busan has Gwangalli beach bars and Seomyeon. Jeju is quiet.

categories.name: Cultural Sights
categories.summary: Busan has Gamcheon Village. Jeju has haenyeo culture.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Busan is base for Gyeongju and Tongyeong. Jeju rewards staying.

faq.question: Is Busan or Jeju better for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: Busan for most - easier transit, no car needed, excellent food and beaches.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Jeju?
faq.answer: Almost certainly yes. Public buses are infrequent. Rental cars 50,000-80,000 KRW/day.

faq.question: Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: Busan is 30-40% cheaper when you factor in Jeju car rental.
